title: Dropping a file far on top of the desktop teleports it to the bottom
line: Dropping a desktop icon past the edge of the screen now puts it in the nearest cell instead of sending it to the opposite side.
explanation: When an icon is moved on the desktop, FolderView.qml turns the drop point into a row and column and then into a linear cell index (row * perStripe + col). A drop above the first cell in column arrangement (or left of it in row arrangement) gave col = -1, so the index wrapped to the last cell of the previous column or row, and the icon jumped to the bottom (or right end). The change clamps the column into the grid and the row to zero or more before computing the cell, so the icon lands in the nearest cell.

commits.message:
containments/desktop: keep dropped icons inside the grid

Dropping an icon past the top or left edge of the desktop gave a
negative cell, which wrapped around to the end of the previous column or
row, so the icon jumped to the far side. Clamp the target into the grid.

BUG: 479085

media.caption: Arrange In Columns: tp2 dragged straight up and dropped at the top edge jumps to the bottom of the previous column
Same drag with the fix: tp2 lands in the top cell of the column it was dropped in

reviews.text: Clean, minimal root-cause fix in FolderView.qml. Clamping `col` to `[0, positioner.perStripe - 1]` and `row` to `>= 0` before computing the linear index `to = (row * positioner.perStripe) + col` stops drops past the top/left edges from wrapping into the far end of the previous column or row, stops drops past the bottom/right edges from leaving `to = -1`, and avoids aborting multi-icon moves on negative `to` while preserving scrollable overflow along the main axis and RTL mirroring. The before/after videos and regression tests clearly prove the fix.

The diagnosis is correct: a drop above the first cell gives col = -1, and row*perStripe + col wraps to the end of the previous stripe. Clamping col to [0, perStripe-1] and row to >= 0 gives the 'nearest cell' the reporter asked for (c13). It covers row mode (c16) and the stacked multi-icon case (c14), and Positioner::move already shifts colliding targets to the next free cell. The before/after videos clearly show the icon jumping to the bottom of the previous column and landing in the top cell with the fix. Drops past the bottom or right edge now go to the nearest cell instead of the first free one, which is consistent and is mentioned in the notes.
